title: Ingest resolution: pluggable ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP classifier at write time
summary: New opt-in IngestResolver protocol classifies each remember() write against its top-k most-similar existing records in scope, mirroring Mem0's real-time ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP pipeline stage — distinct from ENH-3's Reconciler, which only batch-scans for contradictions after the fact.
description:
Add an `IngestResolver` protocol to `types.py`, parallel in shape to `Consolidator`/`Reconciler`: `(candidate, similar: list[tuple[model, distance]]) -> IngestDecision`, where `IngestDecision` names one of `ADD`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`/`NOOP` plus, for `UPDATE`/`DELETE`, the target record id. Ship a `NoOpIngestResolver` default (always `ADD` — today's unchanged behavior). Wire it as an optional `ingest_resolver=` constructor arg on `MemoryStore`; when configured, `remember()` first runs `search()` against the same-type table (scoped, `top_k=resolver_k`) to find similar existing records, passes the candidate plus those results to the resolver, and acts on the decision: `ADD` inserts as today, `UPDATE` calls the existing optimistic-concurrency `update()` on the target id, `DELETE` calls `forget()` on the target id, `NOOP` skips the write entirely.

This is a pipeline stage the SDK doesn't have today: ENH-3's Reconciler runs later, in batches, over already-written non-superseded facts, looking specifically for contradictions between them. This new resolver runs once, at write time, against the top-k most-similar candidates by cosine distance (not a batch scan), and can choose to merge/update/discard/no-op the incoming write itself — the real-time classify-against-existing-similar-memories step Mem0's pipeline is actually built around.

Inspired by: Mem0's three-stage pipeline (extract atomic facts → compare each candidate to top-k existing memories via cosine similarity → an LLM policy routes each to ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NONE), confirmed as still Mem0's core mechanism via 2026 architecture write-ups.

Db2 feasibility: fully feasible — reuses existing `search()`/`update()`/`forget()` machinery, no new schema. Independent of every other story in this epic. Keep this strictly opt-in (`ingest_resolver=None` default) — the 'developer-controlled writes, not mandatory passive extraction' positioning is a deliberate differentiator called out in ai-agent-platform-competitive-analysis.md's SWOT, and this story must not make the default write path any heavier.

comments.text: AUDIT VERIFIED DONE. IngestAction enum, IngestDecision dataclass, IngestResolver Protocol, and NoOpIngestResolver all present in types.py (lines 386–601). MemoryStore constructor accepts ingest_resolver= (default NoOpIngestResolver) and resolver_k= args; remember() fast-paths NoOpIngestResolver and routes to _resolve_and_act() for real resolvers — dispatches ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP using search(), update(), and forget() on the target id. Dedicated test file tests/test_pipe2_ingest_resolver.py covers all four decision paths, edge cases, and the fast-path bypass. 739 unit tests pass.
